This approach prioritizes creating laws that match current technological and social realities over trying to control how people naturally interact and share information.", "summary": "The Swedish Pirate Party insists that legal frameworks must be updated to align with the actual conditions of the digital world, rather than attempting to force outdated rules upon a population whose behavior has already evolved."}, "21": {"original": "Claims the music industry will lose its distribution control and survive only as", "rephrased": "The Swedish Pirate Party predicts that the traditional music industry will inevitably lose its monopoly over distribution channels as non-commercial file sharing becomes widespread, forcing these companies to either transform into value-adding service bureaus for artists or disappear entirely. This shift occurs because the industry currently relies on legal restrictions to act as a middleman, a role that becomes unnecessary and unprofitable when consumers can access music directly.", "summary": "The Swedish Pirate Party predicts that the traditional music industry will inevitably lose its monopoly over distribution channels as non-commercial file sharing becomes widespread, forcing these companies to either transform into value-adding service bureaus for artists or disappear entirely."}, "22": {"original": "Asserts that enforcing copyright in the digital age requires constant monitoring", "rephrased": "The Swedish Pirate Party argues that enforcing strict copyright laws in the modern digital era necessitates the constant surveillance of all private communications, a measure that is both technically unfeasible and a severe violation of personal privacy. Consequently, the party contends that the state cannot realistically police digital file sharing without implementing a surveillance system that would require authorities to monitor every private email and message sent by citizens.", "summary": "The Swedish Pirate Party argues that enforcing strict copyright laws in the modern digital era necessitates the constant surveillance of all private communications, a measure that is both technically unfeasible and a severe violation of personal privacy."}, "23": {"original": "We face a choice: either sacrifice private communications to enforce copyright, ", "rephrased": "The Swedish Pirate Party presents society with a fundamental dilemma: either the state must sacrifice the right to private, unmonitored communications to enforce intellectual property rights, or copyright laws must be reformed to protect the ability to communicate freely.
